# Eval results

<!-- Generated by scripts/eval_report.py from docs/evals/data/. Don't edit by hand. -->

Every case runs in two arms: with the plugin, and without it (the same model and settings, no plugin). LLM graders are judged by Claude Haiku with three votes. The runs happen on the author's machine with Claude Code 2.1.296. Only scores are published: the answers themselves stay on that machine, because they reflect the account that ran them.

- **Score:** the average, over all runs, of the share of scored graders that passed. In the per-case tables, **2/3** means two of three runs passed every grader.
- **Better / same / worse:** cases whose average score is higher, equal or lower with the plugin than without it. A case that also passes without the plugin shows what the model already does well; it still guards against regressions.
- **Right skill fired:** in trigger cases, the share of runs where the expected skill loaded. A trigger-only case checks nothing else, and is left out of the comparison because the plain model can't load a plugin's skill.
- **False triggers:** near-miss runs where one of the plugin's skills loaded although it shouldn't have.

Run them yourself with `just eval <plugin>`, then `just eval-report <result.json>`.

| [`venture-lab`](#venture-lab) | 8 | 3 | 100% | 88% | 1 / 7 / 0 | 100% | 0 of 3 |

Of the 59 cases with work to do (near-misses aside), the plain model alone passed 27 in every run, and 53 passed in every run with the plugins. The plugins did better on 32, the same on 27 and worse on 0.
